# FDG9045

> DO use the suffix “Async” for methods returning `IAsyncEnumerable<T>`.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.2.10 IAsyncEnumerable&lt;T>.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9045
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Add the suffix 'Async' to the name of '{0}', which returns IAsyncEnumerable<T>

FDG9045 reports an externally visible method that returns IAsyncEnumerable<T> and whose name does not end with "Async" or "AsyncCore". It shares its analyzer with FDG9020 and leaves out the same members (overrides, interface implementations, private and internal methods), so coverage is partial. The ValueGenerator examples of FDG9046 lack the suffix; they show the attribute, and they are reported. Renaming a public method breaks its callers, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

Methods that return `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` follow the same naming conventions as methods returning Tasks with the Task-Based Async Pattern, including using the combined suffix “AsyncCore” when making use of the Template Method Pattern (section 9.9).
